newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Short-end vols climb as futures slide.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Short-end vols climb as futures slide.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. interest rate options ended mixed, with Eurodollar volatilities jumping after the yield on the long bond pierced seven percent.
Treasury bond options volatilities continued to trend lower, however, despite the selloff in underlying futures contracts.

June bond volatility slid to 9.44 percent at the end of the shortened trading session, down from 9.66 percent on the opening. Volatility for May options contracts fell harder, to 9.01 percent from 9.60 on the opening.
Traders said the lower bond volatilities reflected widespread sentiment in the market that the seven percent barrier was destined to give way.
Time decay before the long holiday weekend also played a role, with most U.S. trading desks closed Friday and many European traders off Monday as well in observance of the Easter holiday.
"Everyone was waiting for it to happen," a bond trader said.
The yield on the benchmark 30-year cash bond was last trading at 7.09 percent.
In futures, key support levels were broken in June bonds at 108-06 and 107-30 as more evidence of resiliency in the U.S. economy pointed to higher rates ahead.
Activity in the Eurodollar options market began to pick up following news of a jump in February existing home sales, one Eurodollar floor analyst said.

Put buying, especially in short-dated options, was favored as futures sold off, with interest in bearish strategies gaining momentum when the June bond futures contract fell below 107-30, the analyst said.
Eurodollar volatility reversed direction and turned higher at midmorning, gaining 0.2 point on Wednesday's closing levels for quarterly options.

After the close, June volatility was estimated at 8.5 percent, September at 11.9 percent, December at 13.0 percent, March at 14.4 percent, June 1998 at 15.7 percent and September 1998 at 16.5 percent. Mid-curve short-dated June volatility rose 0.5 point to 16.3 percent. Short-dated September was steady, also quoted at 16.3 percent.
